title: implement roi_aligned_rotated
description:
# Current Situation

While managing rotated box, there is no way to perform ROI align pooling for rotated proposals. 

# Expected Situation

Implement and export the mmcv ROI align ops using C++ on CPU.
https://mmcv.readthedocs.io/en/latest/deployment/mmcv_ops_definition.html#mmcvroialignrotated

title: implement box_iou_rotated
description:
# Current Situation

there is no way to operate rotated bbox IoU at scale. 

# Expected Situation

Implement and export the torch/vision ops : https://github.com/pytorch/vision/tree/main/torchvision/csrc/ops : 
 - Implemented Rotated box iou calculation backend using C++ on CPU.
 - Implemented rotated_box_iou function to compute Intersection over Union (IoU) between rotated bounding boxes. 
 - The public API follows the existing box_iou pattern and supports all three rotated box formats: cxcywhr, xywhr, and xyxyxyxy.

Proposed Test Plan: see (https://github.com/pytorch/vision/pull/9379)
Added TestRotatedBoxIou test class with comprehensive tests:

Core IoU test with 4 boxes (including 45° rotated box) across all three formats

Rotation behavior tests (90°, 180°, 45°, negative angles)

Edge case tests (containment, zero area)

API contract tests (output shape, invalid format, format consistency)

title: implement multi-scale deformable attention CUDA ops
description:
As many SoTA networks (RF-DETR, DINO, OpenSeeD) use this attention ops module, I would love to have it available through torchvisionlib.

The CUDA compatible implementation could be inspired from [deformable DETR Torch2 Cuda12](https://github.com/Norman-Ou/Deformable-DETR-Torch2.x-cuda12) or from the original [LW-DETR repository](https://github.com/Atten4Vis/LW-DETR/models/ops/src)

description:
With the brand new {torch} 0.17, we need to close the loop with {torchvisionlib} providing access to pytorch/vision ops matching libtorch version 2.8

Currently torchvisionlib provides access to pytorch/vision [GIT_TAG v0.20.1](https://github.com/mlverse/torchvisionlib/blob/9969cd989da82ae4aaccd057500eaebb83c0fc8d/csrc/CMakeLists.txt#L108)

Libtorch 2.8 match pytorch/vision with **GIT_TAG v0.23.0**, as per https://github.com/pytorch/vision/blob/main/README.md

title: How to adapt the number of classes for pretrained models from the pytorch model zoo?
description:
Hi, I am not sure if this is the correct repo, so let me know if I should it post it somewhere else.
I try to perform transfer learning with `inception_v3` =, but this model is not available in `torchvision` (yet?). According to the readme of this repo it is possible to load pretrained models from PyTorch using jit.

I downloaded the model with a slightly adjusted python script from the readme: 

```
import torch
import torchvision

model = torchvision.models.inception_v3(pretrained = True)
model.eval()

jit_model = torch.jit.script(model)
torch.jit.save(jit_model, 'inception_v3.pt')
```

Then I can load the model into R: 

```
library(torch)
library(torchvisionlib)

# Load the model ----------------------------------------------------------
model <- torch::jit_load(paste0(workspace, "basemodels/inception_v3.pt"))


# Freeze the weights ------------------------------------------------------
coro::loop(for (parameter in model$parameters) {
  parameter$requires_grad <- FALSE
})


# Replace the last layer --------------------------------------------------
# Adapted from https://pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/finetuning_torchvision_models_tutorial.html#inception-v3
model$AuxLogits$fc <- nn_linear(768, num_classes)
```
But that returns this error:

```
model$AuxLogits$fc <- nn_linear(768, num_classes)
Error in `runtime_error()`:
! Script modules can only register Script modules children.
Run `rlang::last_error()` to see where the error occurred.
```
The error message suggests to jit the module, but that gives this error:
```
> model$AuxLogits$fc <- jit_trace_module(nn_linear(768, num_classes), forward = list(torch_randn(num_classes, 768)))
Error in cpp_jit_script_module_register_module(self, name, module) : 
  __torch__.nn_linear_afsxpjxzmpccqmahsyxioaqu (of Python compilation unit at: 000001C5A46995B0) is not compatible with the type __torch__.torch.nn.modules.linear.Linear (of Python compilation unit at: 000001C5B946D6E0) for the field 'fc'
Exception raised from addOrCheckAttribute at C:\actions-runner\_work\pytorch\pytorch\builder\windows\pytorch\aten\src\ATen/core/class_type.h:237 (most recent call first):
00007FFEC0B1DA2200007FFEC0B1D9C0 c10.dll!c10::Error::Error [<unknown file> @ <unknown line number>]
00007FFEC0B1D4AE00007FFEC0B1D460 c10.dll!c10::detail::torchCheckFail [<unknown file> @ <unknown line number>]
00007FFDE126576500007FFDE1265560 torch_cpu.dll!c10::ClassType::addOrCheckAttribute [<unknown file> @ <unknown line number>]
00007FFDE3477C8700007FFDE3477C20 torch_cpu.dll!torch::jit::Module::register_module [<unknown file> @ <unknown line number>]
00007FFE29376DC600007FFE29376CD0 lantern.dll!lantern_ScriptModule_register_module [<unknown file> @ <unknown line number>]
00
```
It seems that it is not possible to overwrite `fc`, but adding a new module and removing the old one works:
```
model$AuxLogits$fc <- NULL
model$AuxLogits$fc_new <- jit_trace_module(nn_linear(768, num_classes), forward = list(torch_randn(num_classes, 768)))
```

However, I am not sure if it then works correctly at the forward pass. 
Do you know how to replace the last layer from a pretrained model downloaded with PyTorch?

I used for R `torch` v0.9.1 and `torchvisionlib` v0.3.0 and at python `torch` v1.12.1

title: Handle non-python builds
description:
It seems that torchvision doesn't really support building the C++ library without linking to Python (see https://github.com/pytorch/vision/issues/2692 ). To handle this we have a few options:

- Patch libtorchvision so it doesn't require linking to Python. I have tried this approach and that wasn't too complicated, only commenting a few `#include <Python.h>` and modifying the cmake build infrastructure to make Python optional. (see https://github.com/dfalbel/vision/commit/2a81375ab31b8eb0ac5f0175e1720f0daff6d64c)
- Vendor the parts of the code that interest us, currently mostly only the `ops` and possibly `io` and arrange our own build system for that. `ops` don't require Python at all, so we would be good with that.
- Ask PyTorch Vision maintainers to support non-python builds. They look interested in doing that given the comments in https://github.com/pytorch/vision/issues/2692 but the issue is sitting since 2020 there.
